problem_text:
A logistics company must select packages to load onto a cargo aircraft. Available shipments are:
* Package 1: volume 7 cubic meters, revenue $102
* Package 2: volume 8 cubic meters, revenue $89
* Package 3: volume 36 cubic meters, revenue $132
* Package 4: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue $257
* Package 5: volume 39 cubic meters, revenue $143
* Package 6: volume 26 cubic meters, revenue $114
* Package 7: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue $277
* Package 8: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $259
* Package 9: volume 5 cubic meters, revenue $126
* Package 10: volume 9 cubic meters, revenue $211
* Package 11: volume 45 cubic meters, revenue $244
* Package 12: volume 5 cubic meters, revenue $136
* Package 13: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue $70
* Package 14: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $232
* Package 15: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue $261
* Package 16: volume 27 cubic meters, revenue $141
* Package 17: volume 39 cubic meters, revenue $108
* Package 18: volume 36 cubic meters, revenue $28
* Package 19: volume 36 cubic meters, revenue $209
* Package 20: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $262
* Package 21: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue $81
* Package 22: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue $167
* Package 23: volume 25 cubic meters, revenue $255
* Package 24: volume 43 cubic meters, revenue $243

The aircraft's cargo hold has a maximum capacity of 399 cubic meters. Choose the package combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each package must be either fully accepted or rejected.
